scenes.heading: Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: What AQE adapts at runtime
items: Switches to broadcast join when a side is small
scenes.narration: Adaptive Query Execution lets Spark re-optimize a query while it runs, using real runtime statistics rather than only planning-time estimates. As shuffles complete, AQE can coalesce many small partitions into fewer, switch a planned sort-merge join to a broadcast join, and split oversized skewed partitions. This closes the gap between what the optimizer guessed and what the data actually looks like.

scenes.heading: How AQE re-plans
scenes.narration: AQE splits execution at shuffle boundaries called query stages. After a stage finishes, Spark reads the true sizes of the shuffle output and feeds them back into the optimizer. The optimizer then adjusts the plan for the remaining stages, choosing better partition counts or join strategies. This loop repeats, so each decision is grounded in observed data.

scenes.code:
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")

res = orders.join(customers, "cust_id").groupBy("region").count()
res.explain()  # AQE nodes appear once the query runs
scenes.heading: Enabling AQE
scenes.narration: These three settings turn on AQE and its two headline features: coalescing shuffle partitions and handling skewed joins. With adaptive enabled, Spark will trim an over-large default shuffle partition count down to what the data needs. The skew setting lets it detect and split lopsided partitions during joins. In Spark 3.2 and later, adaptive execution is on by default.

scenes.heading: Static vs adaptive planning
scenes.narration: Without AQE, the plan is frozen at compile time, so a bad size estimate or an unexpected skew stays with you for the whole job. With AQE, Spark revises those decisions using the sizes it actually observes, coalescing partitions and splitting skew on the fly. The practical payoff is fewer manual tuning knobs and more robust performance across varying data.

scenes.heading: AQE's three optimizations recap
scenes.narration: It helps to hold AQE's three levers together in mind. Partition coalescing merges the many tiny post-shuffle partitions into fewer right-sized ones. The join switch promotes a sort-merge join to a broadcast join once a side proves small at runtime. Skew splitting breaks a lopsided partition into several so no single task lags behind.

scenes.text: Keep AQE enabled; it removes much of the manual shuffle tuning.
scenes.narration: Let AQE right-size shuffle partitions instead of hand-tuning spark.sql.shuffle.partitions for every job.
